query: I have an 81-year-old man. Among male ICU patients aged 76–86 with acute myocardial infarction, stratified by quartiles of distinct procedures in the first 24 hours, report mean procedure count, mean ICU LOS, and hospital mortality (%) for each quartile.
final_sql: SELECT p.gender, i.icu_stay_id, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM i.intime) AS procedure_quarter, COUNT(DISTINCT p.hadm_id) AS patient_count, AVG(i.los) AS average_los, SUM(CASE WHEN p.dod IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT p.hadm_id), 0) AS mortality_rate FROM patients p JOIN admissions a ON p.subject_id = a.subject_id JOIN icustays i ON a.hadm_id = i.subject_id WHERE p.gender = 'M' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM age(CURRENT_DATE, p.dob)) = 81 AND a.admission_type_id = 1 AND i.intime BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '24 hours' AND CURRENT_DATE AND i.dischtime BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE AND CURRENT_DATE + INTERVAL '24 hours' AND p.dod IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.gender, i.icu_stay_id, procedure_quarter ORDER BY p.gender, i.icu_stay_id, procedure_quarter NULLS LAST;
